This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioner mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the Sh. sentences.text: The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the LRs of petitioner are the cobhumidar and is in possession of their share in land bearing Khasra no. 41/5, 42/24; 45/4,7,14,17 total admeasuring 25 bighas and 4 biswas (in short, the said land) as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera,
Delhi.
5. It is stated that the petitioners are entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The ld. LAC has failed in assessing the price of the said land and the said award has been passed amount of which is inadequate, arbitrary, unjust, LAC no. 258 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Dharam Pal v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 illusionary,
without any reasonable aspects, and the award is not acceptable to the petitioner.

sentences.text: 6. It is submitted that the said award has been passed with grave error and the ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the law points involved.

The ld. LAC in assessment of market value of the said land has been guided by the notions and assumptions, rather the reality of the facts points towards a steady rise in the value of the said land owing to largescale purchase of land by private builders, business houses, industrialists on a very cumulative rates during the past several years, therefore, the market value of the said land is higher than the value assessed by the ld. LAC 7.

The ld. LAC has ignored the facts that the said land is surrounded with the land of much higher rates and he has also ignored the facts that the said land was the only source of income of the petitioner, and after acquisition of the said land, the petitioners have become unemployed.

The ld.
LAC has also ignored the fact that the said land is very fertile and having good potential, and commercial crops were sown by the petitioner, and the said land was the only source of income of the petitioner.

The principles for assessment of the market value of land in village Rani Khera and nearby villages/residential areas are not taken into consideration, and prices of land in the vicinity of the said land are much higher than that of the price of the said land assessed by the ld. LAC, at the time of acquisition of the said land.

The assessment of the market value of the said land has been done LAC no. 258 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Dharam Pal v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 arbitrarily by ignoring the principle of natural justice, and if necessary inquiry had been Sh. Dharam Pal S/O(Deceased) Through ... vs Union Of India on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112223756/
2 conducted, the market value of the said land would have not been less than Rs. 10,000/ per square yards.
8.

entities.text: Dharam Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the ld. LAC has totally ignored the facts that the said land is adjacent to the main road which is having well developed farmhouses, main roads and even the railway line is also passing in the vicinity of the said land.
The said land is also very fertile land having great potentiality and substantial value.

The learned LAC has also ignored the facts that all the basic facilities like electricity, water, telephone, banks, post offices, schools, hospital, food supplies office, roads are available in the village Rani Khera.

The ld. LAC has ignored the fact that the said land has great potential and situational value in as much as, on the other side of the land there are residential colonies, which also increases the market value of the said land, and the said land now cannot be termed as agriculture land, however, ld. LAC has failed to appreciate the said fact.

It is submitted that by way of the present petition, the petitioners have sought the increase in market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square yards and the solatium @ 30% along with other additional amount along with interest from the date of notification.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /Union of India and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the Award and and has considered the true prevailing market rates as on the date of notification under Section 4 of the Act.
It is stated that the LAC no. 258 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Dharam Pal v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 Award passed by the ld. LAC is just, legal, proper sufficient and reasonable.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The prices of land situated in the vicinity of the said land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.
11. Vide order dated 12.08.2014, DSIIDC was impleaded as one of the respondents.
However, no written statement was filed on behalf of DSIIDC and vide order dated 15.09.2014, its right to file written submissions was closed.

12. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient, just and legal, and is assessed on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioner to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
20.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Ram Kishan (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
21. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
LAC no. 258 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Dharam Pal v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 22.

entities.text: Dharam Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

23. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioner as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
24. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
LAC no. 258 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Dharam Pal v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 RELIEF 25.

5

(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
26.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
